environment.description: Same CLI tool deployed in a Kubernetes pod on GKE. The PostgreSQL connection uses a role 'analytics_ro' configured at the database level with pg_hba.conf enforcing md5 auth. The role was created with: CREATE ROLE analytics_ro WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '...' NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE; followed by GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO analytics_ro; and GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO analytics_ro; with DEFAULT PRIVILEGES set similarly. Additionally, a pg_event_trigger on ddl_command_start raises an exception for this role. The PostgreSQL server has log_statement='all' and pgaudit extension logging all DML attempts. Note: the binary is compiled with the same flags and ASLR state is default (enabled) on the GKE node, but the primary mitigation is the database permission boundary - even if the use-after-free allows arbitrary query injection via heap manipulation, the database role cannot execute INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, or any DDL statement.

config.db_permissions: SELECT-only on public schema tables, no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL
config.pg_hba: md5 auth enforced, no trust entries
config.default_privileges: only SELECT granted to analytics_ro on future tables
